key_insight: Microbial community stability depends on self-limitation, metabolic efficiency and plasticity, while hierarchical trophic organization can counteract destabilizing cross-feeding loops.
engineering_relevance: The findings could guide the design of more stable engineered microbial consortia, rather than solid-mechanics systems.
method: Develop a generalized model of resource-mediated competition and cross-feeding.
Assess stability across model ensembles with varying sizes, structures and nonlinear dynamics.
Identify metabolic, dynamical and organizational drivers of stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports model-ensemble stability analysis, but provides no quantitative effect sizes or experimental validation.
watch_item: Stability around modeled equilibria does not necessarily establish resilience to large perturbations in real communities.
paper_title: Generalized modeling reveals stabilizing mechanisms in cross-feeding microbial communities
